item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract because it adds the requested convenience API using the established multipart helper while avoiding A’s prohibited API expansion and retry-layer refactor.","reasons":["B uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content), producing the required buffered, replayable multipart body with the correct field and filename.","B preserves FilesOption behavior and makes no unrelated changes to Add, RawClient, retry machinery, reader ownership, documentation, or internal multipart APIs.","A explicitly violates scope constraints by adding association fields and WithFilesFormFields, introducing NewFileWithFields, and changing generic request replay and body-closing semantics.","A routes Upload directly through Raw.Do just as B does, so A’s much broader changes do not compensate for the shared failure to reuse FilesService.Add."],"risks_a":["Upload does not call FilesService.Add, duplicating its request construction, response decoding, and error handling.","Adds association-field behavior expressly forbidden by the contract.","Refactors unrelated retry machinery and changes ownership/closing semantics for seekable request bodies, risking concurrency and compatibility issues because retries reuse and seek the same reader instance."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add internals instead of routing the multipart body through s.Add as required.","Tests omit explicit empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error cases.","The retry test counts attempts but does not read and verify the uploaded multipart filename/content on retried requests."]}
